classification.habitat: Moist valleys, river margins, open forests and cultivated landscapes
classification.distribution: Widely cultivated and naturalized throughout tropical India and other tropical regions

identification.description: A large tree with dense foliage, opposite glossy leaves, white flowers and dark purple to nearly black fleshy fruits.
identification.whole_plant: Large tree with dense rounded crown and dark trunk.
identification.root: Strong woody root system; not usually the primary identifying field character.
identification.stem: Trunk stout with grey-brown to dark bark; older bark may become flaky.
identification.leaf: Opposite, simple, elliptic to oblong leaves, thick and glossy with a characteristic turpentine-like aromatic smell when crushed.
identification.flower: Small white to greenish-white flowers in branched clusters.
identification.fruit: Oblong to ovoid fleshy berries, green when immature and purple-black when ripe, usually with a prominent seed.
identification.seed: Large seed enclosed in the fleshy fruit; commonly one-seeded but variation occurs.
identification.bark: Grey-brown to dark bark; mature bark may show patches or flakes.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Chemical composition differs by plant part and maturity. Published reports commonly discuss anthocyanins, tannins and polyphenols; exact quantitative claims require source-specific verification.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Syzygium cumini is a widely consumed fruit tree and has a substantial traditional and research literature, including studies of fruit, seed and bark. Modern evidence should be interpreted by preparation and clinical endpoint rather than generalized to the whole plant.
modern_information.safety_notes: Traditional use for metabolic conditions should not replace monitoring or prescribed treatment. Verify plant part and preparation.

doctor.quick_reference: Jambu — Syzygium cumini (L.) Skeels; fruit/seed listed as useful in this project record, with traditional indications including Prameha and Atisara.
key_precautions: Verify the plant part and preparation.
Do not substitute traditional Jambu preparations for monitoring or prescribed therapy in metabolic disease.
